builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
summary: The method replaces letting coding agents run until their self-imposed termination by replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and applying stopping or earlier-patch-selection rules. It costs evaluation infrastructure for anytime replay with hidden tests and, for the fine-tuning variant, a training pipeline; the stopping rules themselves are cheap heuristics. Adoption can fail because the preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority: stopping early may discard patch changes that would have repaired the solution, and savings vary sharply by model and scaffold.
rationale: The savings are substantial but quality preservation is unproven, so the reader should validate stopping rules against hidden-test quality on their own model-scaffold combination before production use.
technique: Anytime evaluation of coding-agent stopping rules

claims.statement: The method replaces letting coding agents run until their self-imposed termination by replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and applying stopping or earlier-patch-selection rules. It costs evaluation infrastructure for anytime replay with hidden tests and, for the fine-tuning variant, a training pipeline; the stopping rules themselves are cheap heuristics. Adoption can fail because the preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority: stopping early may discard patch changes that would have repaired the solution, and savings vary sharply by model and scaffold.

Hindsight savings at passing self-tests range from under 1% to 57% depending on model and scaffold; a stop-after-two-passes rule saves 23% in a preregistered replication; fine-tuned imitation saves 30% over six seeds, with quality non-inferiority not established.
